captions.detailed: A tandem stoker crankset featuring a wide, black rectangular bottom-bracket shell in the center. A cylindrical steel spindle passes through the shell, connecting two grey crank arms set 180 degrees apart. The right crank arm includes a single 32T chainring sprocket with pointed teeth. Two black rectangular platform pedals are attached to the outer tips of the crank arms on revolute stub axles, allowing them to spin freely relative to the rotating arms.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a tandem stoker crankset. It should feature a central rectangular bottom-bracket shell, a rotating central spindle, two opposing grey crank arms, a single 32T sprocket chainring on the right arm, and two black rectangular platform pedals that rotate on revolute joints at the arm tips.
captions.factory: The code constructs the crankset by modeling individual rigid parts and defining their articulations. It defines a central 'bb_shell' using a Box primitive. A spindle is modeled as a Cylinder and placed on a revolute joint relative to the shell. Left and right crank arms are designed with custom geometry (extruded profiles or meshes) and fixed to the spindle. A chainring sprocket is attached to the right crank arm. Finally, two rectangular pedals are modeled using Box primitives and connected to the tips of the crank arms via revolute articulations.
